item.title: FiberSurvivors: a browser survivors-like for Fiber (1 posts)
item.description: Hi everyone! I’ve been working on FiberSurvivors, a top-down survivors-like (kinda like Vampire Survivors) that runs in the browser, where the CKB you earn and the upgrade cards you buy are all paid over Fiber. So a run goes like this: You open the game and a Fiber node starts in your browser, with its own wallet You fund it from the testnet faucet Press Play, and the game opens a channel to the hub node (game’s reward liquidity) Clear a level, and the hub pays you CKB Buy upgrade cards mid-run by paying an invoice Cash out at the end, the channel closes and your CKB goes back on-chain All you need is a browser tab, no extension, no local node, no CLI. Everything runs on testnet. The Loop...

item.description: Hi @lestonEth, Thank you for your continued interest in the Spark Program and for submitting the Corven cloud-native IDE proposal. item.title: Spark Program | Spark Verify - Reproducible Acceptance Checks for CKB Projects (1 posts)
item.description: Hello @Akane, Following a review by the Spark Program Committee, your proposal remains Pending. The committee invites you to provide a video demonstration: Based on the written proposal alone, the committee is finding it difficult to accurately assess the tool’s purpose and how it is used. Please create a video (a screen recording is fine) demonstrating and explaining the complete workflow. We’d be happy to help if you need anything. If you have any questions about the committee’s video requirements, please feel free to contact us at any time. We look forward to receiving your demonstration video. Best regards, Xingtian On behalf of the Spark Program Committee

item.title: [DIS] FiberLatch Access - Open-Source Access Control for Fiber Payments (1 posts)
item.description: Post-grant update: FiberFlow integration and real Fiber testnet settlement Hi everyone, I’ve continued working on FiberLatch after the grant, mostly by testing where it can actually fit into existing Fiber applications. One of the projects I tried was FiberFlow. The integration worked around a simple boundary: Fiber payment → FiberFlow invoice.paid → FiberLatch access → protected resource FiberFlow handles the payment. Once the application trusts the paid event, FiberLatch handles the access that comes after it. While testing this, I noticed I was repeating the same PostgreSQL logic in both the FiberFlow integration and a separate FiberLatch reference app, especially around limited-use...

item.title: [DIS] Hardening Kirea Finance (Native RWA Lending on CKB) (2 posts)
item.description: Thanks for reaching out, Salman. I’d like to support you this, but I’d want two things explicitly covered in the hardening milestones. From the current code, the issuer appears able to spend the collateral without consuming the loan cell, bypassing the loan’s release checks. The borrow/repay checks also count output balances rather than net funds received. Could you include enforcing the loan rules on every collateral spend, and verifying actual net disbursement and repayment, with tests covering both? Thanks, Arthur. These are important points, and I agree both need to be explicitly covered in the hardening scope. Milestone 1 is now updated to cover both: Enforcing the loan’s validation...

item.description: CKB Pulse: who is building on CKB, live Hi everyone, We made CKB Pulse, a page that shows the public work on CKB as it happens on GitHub.
